name: CEAAC
funding: DRAC Grand Est, Région Grand Est, Collectivité européenne d'Alsace and the City of Strasbourg. One listed patron, SAS Neunreiter. Residency partners are foreign art centres.
watch: European centre for contemporary artistic action, in the former Neunreiter store. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the about page names the elected board, four public funders, five networks and one patron (SAS Neunreiter), all undated.

name: Crac Occitanie
funding: Run directly by Région Occitanie with the State (Ministry of Culture, DRAC Occitanie). Sète city, Sète Agglopôle and Hérault department are partners.
records_note: Run by Région Occitanie, which posts budgets 2020 to 2026 and names 158 elected councillors; the Crac itself lists only public partners, undated.

name: Kropka (Belarusian community space; listed in place of 'Krokva')
funding: Grants from unnamed international foundations cover about two-thirds of costs; visitor donations; one paid coordinator funded by donor organisations
watch: The brief's 'Krokva' matched no Belarusian cultural space in English, Russian or Belarusian searches (Krokva is a Lahoisk-district village and a surname). Kropka, opened Mar 2022 in Sololaki by Belarusian activists who fled repression, is the closest match: 700+ events and 5,000+ visitors, free coworking, screenings, language clubs, support groups; keeps a deliberately low profile under Georgia's foreign-agent law.
records_note: No site, reports, accounts, funder list or board were found for Kropka, and press says the Tbilisi space closed in January 2025.

name: Ambasada Kultury
funding: German Federal Foreign Office (PerspAKTIV residencies 2022–2025, run with RAZAM e.V. and Galeria Miejska Arsenał, Poznań, earlier Fundacja IN SITU); CEC ArtsLink residency partnership; no full roster published
watch: Initiative of Belarusian culture workers from Minsk, co-founded by former Ў Gallery directors Valiantsina Kisialeva and Hanna Chystaserdava; projects Open Muzej, Antiwarcoalition.art, EVAa, Secondary Archive. CEC ArtsLink lists it as Berlin-based while its own PerspAKTIV page tags it 'Belarus/Lithuania'; no street address is published, so the map point is central Berlin.
records_note: A small initiative with no annual report, accounts or board posted; funders such as the Federal Foreign Office appear only in project credits.

name: Kunstverein Bielefeld
funding: Nearly 1,000 members plus eleven corporate partners: Sparkasse Bielefeld, Hörmann, DMG MORI, Dr. Wolff, Gundlach, Bautra, Wannenmacher, Enderweit, jablgo, PGW Pecunia, Comspace.
watch: Founded 1929 and member-run. No Stadtwerke, energy or arms funder found. Board chair Andreas Wannenmacher.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; the about page lists the five-person Vorstand and shows eleven undated corporate partner logos.

name: Bonner Kunstverein
funding: Project funders: Kunststiftung NRW, NRW culture ministry, Kemmler Foundation, Art Explora.
records_note: No annual report, accounts or funder roster; the about page lists the ten-person Vorstand, and exhibition pages credit funders such as Stadt Bonn per show.

name: Kunstverein für die Rheinlande und Westfalen
funding: City of Düsseldorf and de Haen-Carstanjen & Söhne support it. Stadtwerke Düsseldorf is its permanent partner.
watch: Stadtwerke Düsseldorf is majority-owned by EnBW and runs gas generation.
records_note: The Kunstverein names its eight-person board and advisory board, shows sponsors as undated logos, and posts no annual report or accounts.

name: Kunsthaus Hamburg
funding: Hamburg's Behörde für Kultur und Medien supports it; the Claussen-Simon-Stiftung backed the Whispers show. Part of Kunstmeile Hamburg.
watch: Municipal exhibition hall for contemporary art. The Kemmler Foundation named earlier is on none of the pages opened.
records_note: A non-profit gGmbH that posts no annual report, accounts or board; the home page credits the Hamburg culture authority and Kunstmeile Hamburg by logo.

name: E-WERK Luckenwalde
funding: Kulturstiftung des Bundes, Brandenburg science and culture ministry, Teltow-Fläming district, Mittelbrandenburgische Sparkasse. Kunststrom sales of biomass electricity part-finance the art programme.
watch: Former coal power station now runs on locally sourced biomass. Spanner Re2, a biomass firm, gives support.
records_note: Its site (kunststrom.com) posts no annual report, accounts, funder list or board; the legal notice names only a managing director, Pablo Wendel.

name: Kunsthalle Mainz
funding: Mainzer Stadtwerke and Mainzer Fernwärme head the partner list, with the City of Mainz, Volksbank Darmstadt-Mainz, Rheinhessen Sparkasse and a state ministry.
watch: Main partners are municipal utilities including gas-fired district heating.
records_note: The Kunsthalle names 14 partners with Mainzer Stadtwerke first, but posts no annual report, accounts or board, and its operating foundation lists no officers.

name: Kunsthalle Münster
funding: Municipal institution of the City of Münster's Kulturamt. Residence NRW+ fellowships are paid equally by the NRW culture ministry and Kunststiftung NRW, with Pro Helvetia. A Freundeskreis helps.
watch: No Stadtwerke or arms funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Part of the City of Münster's culture office; the city posts annual accounts 2010 to 2024, while the Kunsthalle lists no funders or board.

name: Haus für Medienkunst Oldenburg
funding: Exhibition house of the City of Oldenburg. Stiftung Niedersachsen pays three media-art grants of €12,500 a year. The building came from donations by Edith Ruß and Elisabeth Brand.
watch: The donors' Nazi pasts came out in early 2024. The council renamed the house from Edith-Russ-Haus on 24 February 2025.
why_flagged: The donors' Nazi pasts came out in early 2024. The council renamed the house from Edith-Russ-Haus on 24 February 2025.
records_note: An exhibition house of the City of Oldenburg: no report, funder list or board of its own, and the city posts annual accounts.
